claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you some key questions about your situation.

**First, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for:**

How old is/are the child/children you want to claim Child Benefit for? Please tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm wanting to claim for my son Alex - he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 9 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into a category where we need to check some additional eligibility criteria. Let me navigate through the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?

(For a 9-year-old, the answer is typically "yes" - children this age are generally not in full-time work. This is just a standard check we need to go through.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's only 9, so he's just in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for a 9-year-old. So Alex is not in paid work at all - he's just in school. Let me move to the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex NOT currently receiving benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?

(Again, for a 9-year-old in school, this is typically "yes" - children don't usually receive these benefits. Just confirming.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So Alex is not receiving any of those benefits himself. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question about Alex:**

Is Alex in an apprenticeship at all? 

(For a 9-year-old in school, this will be "no", but I need to confirm this as it's part of the standard eligibility checks.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in primary school, so he's not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to ask about your residency situation:**

This is an important check. Do any of the following apply to you?

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (with additional criteria about working, job-seeking, having sufficient resources, studying, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these best describes your situation? Or if none of these apply, let me know and we can discuss further.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for clarifying! So you're living abroad. Let me ask a follow-up question to understand your situation better.

**Are you a Crown servant living abroad?** For example, are you:
- Working for the UK government/civil service abroad
- A member of the armed forces stationed abroad
- In a qualifying country as a Crown servant

Or is your situation different - you're just living and working abroad for other reasons?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm just living abroad for other reasons.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So you're living abroad but you're not a Crown servant. I need to ask a bit more to understand your residency status fully.

**Do you have any of the following statuses?**

1. **Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you were an EU/EEA national who applied and received settled status
2. **Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you were an EU/EEA national who applied and received pre-settled status
3. **Neither of the above** - You're a British citizen or have a different immigration status

Which applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Neither of those - I'm a British citizen, I'm just living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. As a British citizen living abroad, I need to ask an important follow-up question:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Even though you're currently living abroad, the eligibility rules ask whether you "normally" live in the UK. This can include:
- You lived in the UK and have just temporarily moved abroad (for work, a sabbatical, etc.) and plan to return
- You have a permanent home in the UK even though you're abroad at the moment
- Your centre of interests (family, work, home) is still in the UK

Or do you consider yourself to have permanently relocated abroad, without plans to return?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I've permanently relocated - I don't have plans to return to the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being clear about that. Unfortunately, this means you don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

The UK Child Benefit rules require that the claimant **normally lives in the UK**. Since you've permanently relocated abroad and don't plan to return, you don't meet this fundamental requirement.

Let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Summary:**
- **Child:** Alex (age 9)
- **Eligibility:** NOT eligible for Child Benefit
- **Reason:** While Alex would otherwise qualify (he's under 16, not in full-time work, not receiving disqualifying benefits, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship), the key issue is that **you do not meet the UK residency requirement**. Child Benefit requires the claimant to normally live in the UK, and your permanent relocation abroad means you don't satisfy this requirement.

**What you might want to know:**
- If your circumstances change and you return to the UK to live permanently, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex (subject to other eligibility criteria at that time)
- You may want to check if there are any other benefits or support available to you in the country where you're currently living
- For specific advice about your situation, you can contact HMRC on 0300 200 3100 or visit www.gov.uk/child-benefit

I'm sorry this wasn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about the Child Benefit rules?

reasonings: Alex is 9 years old (under 16, which is a qualifying age). He is not working full-time, is not receiving benefits in his own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. However, the claimant (his parent) does not meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant has permanently relocated abroad and does not normally live in the UK. Child Benefit requires the claimant to normally reside in the UK, which is not satisfied in this case. Therefore, Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: While Alex would otherwise qualify for Child Benefit as a 9-year-old child not in full-time work or receiving disqualifying benefits, the claimant's permanent relocation abroad means they do not meet the UK residency requirement. The claimant must normally live in the UK to claim Child Benefit for their child(ren)."
